title: Helper steps
description: The protocol between an agent that works through helpers (the lead agent), the helpers it starts or plans, and the script that runs the step journal. The lead agent records its helpers as child steps of its own step with `atw-step-journal` (step-journal.schema.json is the journal's shape; the plans it adds are step-journal.schema.json#/definitions/stepPlan). The instance this file validates is the list of child steps under the lead agent's step, in order: every helper step, then one step whose description begins `Finish`, performed by the lead agent itself. The fixed names below are the ones the script reads; orchestrator/flows/architecture_files.py holds them as constants. Order and recording: (1) the lead agent writes its own first output before it adds any step; (2) it adds each helper as a child before `Finish` (`atw-step-journal add --parent <own step>`, a later one with `--after <sibling id>`), and `Finish` as the last child, with its own step in the inputs of `Finish`; (3) a helper it starts in its own session is marked running (`atw-step-journal start`) and its request file is recorded at once under the artifact name `request` (or `question`); when the helper returns, its file is recorded as `answer` and the child is marked done. Helpers that do not depend on each other form one round: the lead agent adds each as a child, marks each running and records each request, and only then starts them all at once, as concurrent calls in one message; no helper of a round waits on a sibling; (4) its result is recorded on `Finish` under the name its definition gives, and `Finish` is marked done. A helper the lead agent only plans for the script to run gets its request file recorded on the lead agent's own step under the same names, and names that step in its inputs. After an interruption the script runs the first child that is not done: a helper whose answer file is already on disk, valid and written since its step started, is recorded done without being started again; any other helper is started from the `request` file its step holds; `Finish` is started as the lead agent, which reads its own output, the `answer` files and its partial result, and continues. A step is handed the artifacts of the steps its inputs name, and of the steps below them.

ChildStep.description: One child step under the lead agent's step: a helper, or the closing step whose description begins `Finish`.

description.description: What the step does. The closing step's description begins with `Finish` (x-finish).

agent.description: The helper's own agent name, as its definition's `name` states it; for `Finish`, the lead agent's own name.

artifacts.description: What the step records, by the fixed names.

ArtifactName.description: The fixed names of the files a helper step holds; the script reads them by these names.

oneOf.description: What a helper is asked, written by the lead agent before the helper starts.
A question file to architecture-question.schema.json, in place of `request`, for the architecture decider.
What a helper or design specialist returned, at the request's answer path.
What the architecture maintainer is asked to write (write-request.schema.json).
